title: Kernel fusion + scheduler behavior for long-context and MoE models (Llama / Mistral / Qwen) - probe log
content:
Purpose:
This is an exploratory probe into the interaction between kernel-level fusion optimizations and the request scheduler when serving long-context workloads across Llama, Mistral and Qwen family models, with a specific look at MoE routing effects. Goal is to surface counterintuitive perf regressions we've seen on 16k+ contexts and to capture actionable hypotheses for the serving runtime (fusion config, scheduler policy, prefetch hooks).

Summary of findings (high level):
- Kernel fusion improves single-token compute for standard MHA/QKV sequences, but for long-context workloads (>16k) fusion can increase register pressure and reduce SM occupancy on H100 for Qwen variants, resulting in worse p50 and p95 latencies.
- When MoE routing is present, the scheduler's multi-GPU dispatch combined with synchronous prefetch of expert weights causes PCIe/NVLink contention and stalls; moving routing decisions earlier and allowing asynchronous prefetch reduced stalls in our traces.
- A hybrid scheduler that prefers co-location of MoE routing + attention compute on the same GPU (when capacity allows) reduced cross-GPU transfers and improved throughput by ~12% on A100 clusters in our tests.

Environment and baseline config:
- Hardware: 4x A100 80GB (NVLink), 2x H100 80GB (NVLink) testbeds
- Serving runtime baseline: branch main@2025-09 + local perf flags (continuous-batching enabled, prefix-caching on)
- Models: llama-3b-16k, mistral-7b-long, qwen-14b-32k, moe-8e-16k (experimental gating)
- Input profiles: short chat (<=512), medium doc (2k-8k), long-context (16k-32k)
- Workload: steady-state mixed QPS targeting 60-80% cluster capacity to expose queuing and scheduler behavior

Experiment logs (selected):
1) Experiment KF-SCHED-01: kernel fusion toggles on H100, qwen-14b-32k
   - Config: fused-MHA=on, fused-qkv-pack=on, tile-size=128
   - Observation: p50 increased 7% and p95 increased 18% vs fusion=off. GPU SM occupancy dropped from 85%->62%. Register spill increased (nvprof shows spill stores up 3x).
   - Hypothesis: aggressive fusion increases per-thread register usage for Qwen attention implementation with long KV sequences, causing register spilling and memory traffic overhead that dominates compute savings.

2) Experiment KF-SCHED-02: same as 01 but with tile-size reduced to 64 and partial-fusion strategy
   - Result: p50 improved 9% relative to fusion=on (tile128) and matched fusion=off latency; occupancy up to 76%.
   - Takeaway: smaller microkernel tiles reduce register pressure; adaptive tile selection by sequence-length could be beneficial.

3) Experiment MOE-SCHED-03: MoE routing dispatch behavior across 4xA100, mixed long-context requests
   - Baseline scheduler: round-robin GPU assignment, routing computed after initial token precompute, prefetch experts synchronously when route assigned.
   - Symptom: intermittent 200-500ms stalls correlated with NVLink counters and blocked memcpy ops in traces.
   - Intervention: move gating decision into pre-scheduling phase (compute route in CPU scheduling path), then asynchronously prefetch top-K experts with non-blocking transfers before main attention+FFN.
   - Result: p95 tail reduced by ~30-40% for long-context MoE requests; throughput increased ~12% for MoE-heavy mixes.

4) Experiment PREFETCH-04: prefix/KV cache interactions with fused kernels
   - Issue: fused attention kernels expect contiguous KV layout; our prefix-caching splits KV pages across buffers, causing additional memcpy to consolidate before kernel call. Fused kernel time saved was offset by consolidation copies for long contexts.
   - Quick hack: add in-place consolidation path where cache writes back into contiguous slab; reduced memcpy overhead by ~60% and restored net gains from fusion for medium-long contexts.

Profiles and traces pointers:
- perf traces stored under perf-drive (link in linked_artifacts). Key files: traces/kf-sched-01.nvprof (H100), traces/moe-sched-03.nvlink.csv (A100 NVLink counters).
- Flamegraphs show increased memcpy activity between fused kernel launches for long-context cases.

Open hypotheses and questions to validate:
- Is register pressure the dominant factor for all Qwen variants or only for the qwen-14b attention implementation? Need per-layer register / liveness stats.
- Can we make fusion adaptive on a per-request basis (sequence length + model heuristics)? Costs: compile cache churn vs latency wins.
- For MoE, is co-location (routing + experts) always better? Edge cases: when expert hotness would cause one GPU to become overloaded — need cost model (latency vs transfer cost).
- Interaction with continuous batching: does batching combined with fusion amplify register/memory pressure? Some traces suggest increased spill when two long-context requests are merged in a single batch.

Immediate actionable items (short-term):
- Implement microkernel tile-size tuning knob exposed to scheduler; add heuristics: tile=64 for seq>8192 for Qwen builds. (Owner: Owen)
- Add async prefetch path for MoE experts in scheduler; gating decision earlier in CPU scheduling pipeline. (Owner: Ravi)
- Add a small consolidation path for KV cache to satisfy fused kernel contiguous requirement without full memcpy. (Owner: Maya)
- Add a perf CI job that runs a minimal long-context fusion smoke test on H100 with register/spill metrics reported. (Owner: Ava)

Longer-term investigations:
- Explore compiler-level register allocation tradeoffs for fused kernels (LLVM passes or Triton heuristics).
- Evaluate dynamic fusion decision at runtime using a cheap estimator of register pressure (e.g., per-layer FLOP-to-reg estimate).
- Study scheduling policy that balances co-location for MoE against global load (cost model + simulated annealing placement).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a working document; many experiments are exploratory and parameter sweeps. Please comment if you have perf traces I missed (esp. H100-specific nvprof outputs).
- Related tickets: JIRA-PERF-842 (kernel-fusion regressions), JIRA-MOE-519 (routing prefetch).
- Prior art: similar fusion/regression noted in 2025-06 internal note (see confluence link), but this probe adds MoE scheduling interplay which we hadn't isolated before.

Appendix: quick measurement table (single-run numbers, synthetic input, p50/p95 in ms):
- qwen-14b-32k, fusion=on (tile128): p50=420ms, p95=940ms, occupancy=62%
- qwen-14b-32k, fusion=off: p50=390ms, p95=800ms, occupancy=85%
- qwen-14b-32k, fusion=on (tile64): p50=355ms, p95=780ms, occupancy=76%
- moe-8e-16k, baseline-scheduler: throughput=22 rps, p95=1.3s
- moe-8e-16k, async-prefetch + co-locate: throughput=24.6 rps, p95=0.85s

Next steps before marking final:
- Re-run KF-SCHED-01/02 on H100 and A100 with deterministic seeds and attach nvprof/nvlink counters in perf artifacts.
- Prototype scheduler heuristics (tile-size + async prefetch) behind runtime flags; roll to internal staging and measure against CI long-context job.

End of probe log.

(Notes-to-self: remember to push small repro harness for qwen-14b with seq=32k to perf sandbox so others can reproduce register spill behaviour.)
